_comment: EVERY CLAIM HERE WAS DRIVEN ON THE CUSTOMER PATH, AND NAMES THE ARTIFACT VERSION IT WAS DRIVEN AGAINST.
check-credential-claims-remeasured.mjs fails when a newer version of that artifact publishes, because
the claim then describes bytes nobody has checked. Re-drive it, then move the version here.
Do not edit a version in this file without re-driving the arm it refers to: the version IS the claim
that someone looked.

A claim with driven_by is REPRODUCED ON TODAY'S BYTES by that script, so its measured_version is history rather than a promise and this check does not grade it. Refusal arms can be driven for free -- no credential, no render, nothing billed -- so they are not attested at all. Claims WITHOUT driven_by need a credential or a device to prove, and there the version field is the claim that a human looked.
HOW TO KNOW YOUR RE-DRIVE IS COMPARABLE. Three controls, answering three different questions.
1. POSITIVE CONTROL — can the instrument see anything at all? Search for a string you know is
present, in the SAME sweep. A zero from a blind instrument looks exactly like a real zero:
ugrep's -l prints nothing for a binary match, and that nearly put a false claim on a page.
2. DIFFERENTIAL — can it see THIS string in THIS artifact shape? Run the same method against the
version that still HAS the property. Needed for any 'X is gone' claim: it proves the absence is
the artifact and not the search.
3. BACK-MEASUREMENT — does your recipe reproduce the number you are about to REPLACE? Run your
method against the OLD artifact and check you get the figure already written down. Needed for
any 'unchanged' or 'superseded' claim. Nobody runs it, because re-deriving a number you already
believe feels like work for nothing — right up until the two recipes disagree, at which point
'unchanged' was two methods agreeing by luck, which is indistinguishable from a property holding.
Landed 2026-09-15 after all three were needed in one night: (1) on the Android AAR, (2) on 0.5.6
vs 0.5.7, (3) on the LGPL symbol count before moving that page from 0.5.6 to 0.5.7.
EVERY CLAIM CARRIES A `route`, AND THE CHECK REFUSES WITHOUT ONE. It names the invocation and code path
actually driven — not the command, the ROUTE. This exists because of a real handoff on 2026-09-15: a lane
reported livekit-server as required for `bithuman run`, with a measured refusal, an exact error string, a
machine name and an exit code. All true. The missing qualifier was WHICH ROUTE REACHES IT — on the published
CLI an expression-2 model is routed away from serve and never meets LiveKit at all. The author had read that
routing line by line and compressed it out at the handoff, because by then it was background to them rather
than news. ★A handoff is where the author's context is richest and the reader's is poorest, and compression
runs the wrong way at exactly that point. This field cannot check that a route is RIGHT. It checks that one
was STATED, which turns omission-by-familiarity into a blank instead of confident prose.

REAL credential + the same unreachable base + ENFORCE=1: sign-in passes, 'embedded livekit-server up', first-run brain venv built (pip: bithuman 2.11.3 + livekit-agents 1.5.12), 'embedded agent-worker brain up', 'bithuman is live: http://127.0.0.1:18094/WISEPUP'. NEW ON 2.6.23 — the first-frame question the 2.6.22 record left open is now measured: a GET of /WISEPUP (which POSTs /launch) rendered 74 frames with the meter unreachable and ENFORCE=1 set — '[selfhost-meter] could not reach https://meter-unreachable.invalid/v1/auth/validate … PROCEEDING and metering in the background', 'beat seq=1 failed to send … 5.7s (74 frames) stay UNACKED and will be re-claimed. Rendering continues.', session closed 'beats delivered=0 failed=1 frames=74'. So on Linux the variable refuses nothing at the first frame either. Control on the same bytes with the REAL API base: a viewer launch rendered 138 frames and the meter delivered ('beat seq=1 served=10.6s product=expression-2 delivered (final)', 'beats delivered=1 failed=0'). macOS arm64 NOT re-driven on 2.6.23 (the 2.6.22 macOS arms: sign-in exit 1 identical; real credential live). The 2.6.20 figure (macOS 77 / Linux 120 frames) came from the preview path, which 2.6.21+ no longer has.

The no-credential route is a different claim (driven by check-cli-refusals.mjs).
